subtype: Approach: building an emergency fund first [Action]
passage: In their two-room rented home in a mill town, Ujjwal and Sabina both wanted a small plot and a scooter. "First," Sabina said, "six months of what we spend, in an account we can reach any day." It took two years, setting aside a fixed sum on the day the salary arrived. Then the mill announced a shutdown for repairs, and Ujjwal was sent home without pay for two months. He sat on the doorstep, quiet. Sabina brought tea and the bank passbook. "We can manage." They paid rent and food from the fund and asked nobody for a loan. When the mill reopened, they started on the plot fund again, a little wiser and a lot calmer.

qa.q: How many months of spending did Sabina want in the account first?
qa.a: Sabina wanted six months of what they spend.

qa.q: How was Ujjwal feeling when he sat quietly on the doorstep?
qa.a: Ujjwal was worried and low after the mill sent him home without pay, until Sabina showed the passbook and said they could manage.

qa.q: What else could the couple do with the fund, and why?
qa.a: They could keep it apart from everyday money and check it once a year, because money that is easy to reach for other things may not be there in an emergency.

qa.q: How might Sabina have felt handing over the passbook?
qa.a: Sabina was probably relieved and quietly proud that the years of setting money aside had paid off.

grounding: Illustrates a couple holding six months of expenses in an easily reached account before big goals, so a job scare later passes without borrowing.

subtype: Approach: building an emergency fund first [Action]
passage:
When Valentina and Emeka got married in Madrid, their friends were buying flats and cars. They made a different first decision.
On their first Sunday as a married couple, at the kitchen table, they added up what they spent in a normal month: rent, food, transport, phone. Then they agreed that before any big goal, they would build a reserve worth six months of that, kept in a savings account they could get to quickly.
It took them almost two years. Valentina moved to a cheaper phone plan. Emeka cycled to work in spring.
Last October, Emeka's company announced layoffs. For three weeks nobody knew who would stay. Emeka couldn't sleep.
Valentina put the reserve statement on the fridge with a magnet. "Look. Six months. Whatever happens, we're fine for a while."
He kept his job in the end. But he still remembers how that piece of paper made him breathe.

qa.q: How long did it take Valentina and Emeka to build the reserve?
How did Emeka feel during the three weeks of layoff uncertainty?
qa.a: Emeka was anxious and couldn't sleep, then felt calmer and reassured when he saw the reserve statement.

qa.q: What else could Valentina and Emeka do now that the scare has passed?
qa.a: They could talk together about their next big goal, and speak to a qualified adviser if they want help comparing options.

qa.q: How did the reserve look to Valentina during the layoff scare?
qa.a: Valentina felt steady enough to comfort Emeka, because the reserve gave them time whatever happened.

grounding: It shows a couple choosing to hold six months of expenses in an accessible account before big goals, which lets them get through a job scare without borrowing.

subtype: Approach: building an emergency fund first [Action]
passage:
The staff canteen at the Bhubaneswar hospital was nearly empty when Rukmini, a staff nurse, sat down across from her husband Arnab, who worked in the hospital's accounts office.
"The trust announced a hiring freeze and job cuts in admin," Arnab said quietly. "My section is on the list for review."
Rukmini put her tea down. Then she took a breath. "Arnab, remember the first year? We said, no flat, no car, until we had six months of our expenses in the account we can use any time."
"I remember. You made us cancel the trip to Darjeeling."
"And it's there now. Six months."
They sat for a moment. Arnab's shoulders came down a little.
Three weeks later, he was told his post would be cut. It took him four months to find a new job at a college. They didn't borrow from anyone. They didn't even touch the last two months of the reserve.

qa.q: How long did it take Arnab to find a new job?
How did Arnab feel when he first told Rukmini about the job cuts, and what changed?
qa.a: He was anxious and tense, speaking quietly, but his shoulders came down a little when she reminded him of the reserve, showing some relief.

qa.q: What else could the couple do after Arnab found the new job?
qa.a: They could talk together about rebuilding the reserve and their next goals, and ask a qualified adviser if they want help with options.

qa.q: How did the reserve look to Rukmini during the uncertain months?
qa.a: Rukmini could stay steady and reassure Arnab, since the reserve they built early meant they could get through without borrowing.

grounding: It shows a couple building six months of expenses in an easy-to-reach account before big goals, which helps them through a job loss without borrowing.
